I'm examining the sequence around residue 348 in chain B, which resembles a zinc finger DNA-binding domain of a nuclear receptor, trying to figure out the secondary structure in that region.

I'm mapping out the residue-by-residue numbering of this zinc-finger DNA-binding domain sequence, trying to pin down which nuclear receptor family member it matches, possibly Nurr1 or another NR4A member.

I'm shifting to check actual geometry now, looking up CA coordinates for residues around 341-344 to compute distances directly rather than relying on sequence alignment alone.

Checking consecutive CA-CA distances confirms most are within normal bonded range around 3.8 Å. I'm also checking a longer-range distance between residues 348 and 353 to see if they might form part of a beta strand pairing.

Not finding good pairing at 349-352 either. I'm now thinking about the nuclear receptor DBD architecture, recalling that this region contains two zinc-finger modules followed by helices — the recognition helix around residues 321-333, and a second helix following the second zinc module — rather than a canonical beta-sheet, so I should focus on identifying these helical segments instead of forcing a strand pairing.

I'm checking the CA-to-CA distances for a possible hairpin turn around residues 349-354, and testing whether the 345-352 stretch forms a helix by comparing i to i+4 spacing against the expected ~6.2 Å, but the region looks too extended for that.

Extending the check to 346-351 confirms distances closer to beta-strand spacing (~6.3-7 Å) rather than helical, so this looks like an extended segment. Now I need to verify if it's an actual paired strand by looking for H-bond partners, checking residues 341-344 as a potential pairing region.

Checking 366's CA position confirms it's too far in z to pair with 348. Scanning nearby residues like 304 and 353, nothing falls within typical strand-pairing distance—353 is closest at 6.77 Å, well beyond the ~4.5-5 Å expected for beta-sheet pairing. This suggests 348 isn't part of a paired strand, so I should verify by checking backbone H-bond distances between 348 and 353 directly.

The N-O distance between 348 and 353 comes out to about 6.6 Å, too far for a hydrogen bond, confirming no beta bridge. I also check if it could be helical instead by testing the O-N distance between 348 and 352, but that's also far, ruling out helix. So this residue should be classified as coil.
